newsitem.title: USA: Key Energy to acquire Nabors service unit.
newsitem.headline: Key Energy to acquire Nabors service unit.

text.p: Key Energy Group Inc said Monday it has agreed to acquire J.W. Gibson Well Service Co from Nabors Industries Inc for cash, stock and warrants with an estimated value of $25.0 million.
Key said it also has signed a letter of intent to acquire Dunbar Well Service Inc for $10.0 million, consisting of $11.8 million of cash, less $1.8 million of working capital.

Management believes that, following the closing of pending acquisitions, the company will become the largest domestic well servicing company based on revenues, equipment in service and the size of its ancillary well service operations.
Key said its pro forma annualized revenues following the pending acquisitions are estimated to be about $330 million.

It said the purchase of Gibson and Dunbar, combined with the recently announced acquisitions of Patrick Well Service, Kenting Holdings (Argentina), Mosley Well Service, Big A Well Service, Ram Oilwell Service and Rowland Trucking, will increase the company's total well service/workover rig count to 714 rigs and 603 fluid hauling trucks.
Chairman Francis John Chairman said, "The acquisition of Gibson and Dunbar represent the final steps in the first phase of Key Energy's domestic consolidation strategy."

"Upon commencing the first phase in our acquisition strategy, we targeted several regions and specific operations which we felt would make perfect complements to our existing assets. We believe that we have far exceeded even our best expectations in this regard," John said.

"We will now focus on further integrating all of the acquired companies and further enhancing our industry high margins to create substantial incremental shareholder value and to best position Key Energy for what is widely viewed as the beginning of a very strong period for the domestic onshore service industry."
Closing of the Gibson acquisition is expected in October and Key Energy will manage the operations of Gibson in the interim, Key said.
Spokesman Jim Dean said the payment to Nabors includes $20 million in cash, 100,000 Key common shares and 265,000 warrants to purchase Key common.
Completion of the Dunbar acquistion is subject to the negotiation of a definitive agreement, the company's standard due diligence and any regulatory approvals.
Gibson, based in Englewood, Colo., operates 74 well service and workover rigs, which is the fourth largest domestic fleet, out of fourteen yards in eight states.
The purchase price includes 16 fluid hauling and other trucks, 35 pumps, 17 power swivels, 22 blowout preventers, roustabout equipment and miscellaneous support equipment.
Key said Gibson is expected to contribute revenues of about $32 million a year based on historical levels of revenues and will have no debt when acquired.

Dunbar, based in Gillette, Wyo., operates 38 well service and workover rigs out of nine yards in Wyoming. The purchase price includes 30 pumps, 16 power swivels, and other auxiliary equipment. Dunbar is expected to contribute revenues of $11 million a year based on historical levels of revenues and will have no debt when acquired.
Key Energy also said it has completed the previously announced acquisition of Kenting Holdings (Argentina) SA from Precision Drilling Corp for $10.1 million in cash.
